newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks call time out after big gains.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks call time out after big gains.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell on profit-taking Thursday, pausing after their fast-paced recovery in the last three days.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 48.97 points at 6,960.02, retreating somewhat after soaring 265 points since the start of the week.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 13-9 on volume of 267 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite Index gained 8.14 to 1,268.90.
Analysts said investors were wary ahead of the April employment report, which is due on Friday.

"The Dow's pullback can be accounted for," said Anthony O'Bryan, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons. "The average deserves a rest because blue chips have been so strong lately and were vulnerable to some very normal profit-taking.
"Also, the employment report is critical. It ranks with the employment cost index as the indicator that (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan watches," he said.

Stocks retreated despite a strong bond market. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 12/32, sending its yield down to 6.93 percent from Wednesday's 6.96 percent. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.
The bond market responded to the National Association of Purchasing Management's report that its index of manufacturing activity fell to 54.2 in April from 55.0 in March.
The NAPM's price index also was lower, slipping to 49.6 from 50.9 as commodities purchased by manufacturers were cheaper.

The slowdown in manufacturing activity and the drop in prices heightened expectations that the Federal Reserve would hold off from raising interest rates again at its policy-setting meeting on May 20.
O'Bryan said the stock market was fickle and people were taking some of their big profits off the table lest Friday's report change the mood yet again.
"Everyone's mind-set changes quickly. Everyone was bearish a week ago. Now they are bullish. You get a terrible number tomorrow and everyone might start selling again," he said.
The rally in technology stocks extended to small-name companies, which have been overlooked during the recent market recovery.
Micron Technology Inc., the most actively traded NYSE issue, was up 2 at 37-1/4. Cisco Systems Inc. gained 1-3/8 at 53-1/8, Adobe Systems was up 2-7/16 at 41-9/16, 3Com Corp. was up 2-1/8 at 31-1/8.
Cigna Corp. rose 4-1/4 to 154-5/8 after the company posted better-than-expected first quarter profits.
